sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wondered how Java handles numbers that don't quite fit? Let's explore type casting - your tool to convert between data types!

• What type casting is and why it matters
• How to widen and narrow data types
• Common pitfalls and how to avoid them

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you're pouring liquids between containers:
- A small cup (int) can easily fit into a large pitcher (double) - that's widening!
- But pouring a pitcher into a cup? You might spill some - that's narrowing, and you need to be careful!

Type casting works the same way with numbers in Java:
• **Widening**: Safe, automatic conversion (e.g., int → double)
  - Java does this for you behind the scenes
  - No data loss occurs

• **Narrowing**: Risky, manual conversion (e.g., double → int)
  - You must explicitly tell Java to do this
  - Can lose data (like decimal places)

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Widening casting (implicit) converts a smaller type to a larger type without data loss
Narrowing casting (explicit) requires a cast operator and may lose data: (int) 3.9 yields 3
Casting in expressions: (double) a / b forces floating-point division
The promotion order is: byte -> short -> int -> long -> float -> double
Always cast explicitly when narrowing to make the intent clear and avoid compiler errors

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Type casting converts between data types. Widening = safe & automatic; Narrowing = risky & manual. Practice casting with different numeric types. Ready to handle user input next.
